known_facts_book1: Queen of the one hundred and one Skeezers, a girl of about fifteen or sixteen, too thin and plain of feature to be pretty, with black hair, white skin and black eyes, elaborately dressed and enormously proud.
Calls herself a **Krumbic Witch**, the only one in the world, and claims to fear the magic of no other creature.
**Stole all her magic**: she invited the three Adepts at Magic to a banquet, took their charms and instruments, transformed them into a gold, a silver and a bronze fish, and threw them into the lake.

Was warned by one of the fishes that if any one of them dies or is destroyed she will become shrivelled and helpless and all her stolen magic will depart — which is why she threw them into the water alive.
Was not a magic-worker at all before that, and knew nothing to be proud of; the Adepts had been kind to her and built the Skeezers their glass Dome and marble houses.
Can hear **every word spoken on the island**, even the slightest whisper, and has her people lashed at a whipping post with knotted cords for talking about her in their own homes.
Transformed Rora Flathead into a Golden Pig, in the act of poisoning the lake's fishes, and took away Rora's four cans of brains as well.
Has a **Magic Oracle**, which tells her who Ozma and Dorothy are before they ever speak.
Submerges the entire island rather than fight on the surface, and keeps several **submarines** in little rooms in the basement, moved not by machinery but by spoken words she alone knows.

Is defeated in one instant: raising her silver rope to throw at the Su-dic, she takes a copper vessel of contents full in the face and rises from the lake as a **Diamond Swan** — white feathers thick with tiny diamonds, a golden bill, amethyst eyes.
**Forgets all her magic with the transformation**, and is glad of it: her past life seems an unpleasant dream she would not go back to.
Abandons her people completely, ignoring Ervic's pleas, and swims off to admire her own reflection.
Cannot be bribed with a string of pearls to recall how to raise the island, because nothing can add to her beauty.
Is never disenchanted: she remains a swan at the end of the book, and Glinda calls that punishment enough, since she has lost her magic, her palace and her power to misrule.

known_relations_book1.Lady Aurex: Her lady in waiting, who witnessed the betrayal and later replaces her.

Coo-ee-oh is an ally of the three Adepts

known_facts_book1: A Skeezer lady in waiting on Queen Coo-ee-oh, about twenty in appearance, with a pleasant attractive face that is solemn and sad like every Skeezer's.
Is ordered to house Ozma and Dorothy and care for them, and does so kindly — they are prisoners, but treated with much consideration.
Dares not speak freely at first, because the Queen hears everything and punishes remarks she does not like; she speaks only after Ozma enchants the house.
**Witnessed the betrayal of the three Adepts herself**, along with many other Skeezers, and it is her account that explains the whole quarrel.
Says the Skeezers are not bad people and do not care to quarrel even with the Flatheads, but are so cowed they obey Coo-ee-oh's slightest word.
Almost wishes the Flatheads would conquer, to be free of the Queen — but not at the cost of the three fishes, in whom lies the Skeezers' only hope of future happiness.
Knows how the Dome, the submarines and the doors work, and knows equally that no one but Coo-ee-oh can operate any of them.
Is **elected Queen** by the Skeezers themselves once Ozma offers them the choice, and is crowned the same day.
Chooses **Ervic as her Prime Minister**, on the Adepts' testimony of his good judgment, faithfulness and cleverness.
Fears only one thing at the end — the enmity of the Su-dic — and is reassured by Ozma's promise to stop at the mountain on the way home.

known_facts_book1: A young Skeezer, leader of the four men Coo-ee-oh took with her in the submarine, and the only one of the four who does anything at all in the book.
Pleads with the Diamond Swan four times for the way back to the island and gets only boasts about her own beauty in reply.
Volunteers to stay awake and watch while his three comrades sleep, and so is the only one to see the three fishes rise beside the boat.
Ties Coo-ee-oh's dropped **silver cord** to the bow, and the three small fishes drag the iron boat to the shore.

Scrubs the Su-dic's forgotten **copper kettle** clean of poison with sand, fills it with fresh water, and carries the three fishes in it a hundred steps east and then miles overland to a purple cottage — warned that spilling the water would destroy them.
Walks into Reera the Yookoohoo's cottage past a crocodile, giant spiders, horned toads, black rats and a fire-spitting lizard, and refuses to be moved from his bench by any of them.
**Disarms Reera by wanting nothing**: he asks no favor, expects nothing, and is not afraid — an attitude no visitor of hers had ever taken, and the reason she tolerates him.
Runs the whole deception in reverse: he loudly objects to the fishes being transformed, suggests only in passing that girls who were *Adepts at Magic* might please him, and lets Reera insist.
Is stopped by the fishes from stealing the magic powder out of Reera's cupboard drawer — only the Yookoohoo knows how to use it, and his deception was already working.
Lies twice, plausibly: that the fishes are pets for a friend's three children, and that they were asking for bread.
Keeps his promise never to tell who restored the Adepts, so Glinda never learns it was Reera.
Is made **Prime Minister** of the Skeezers by Queen Aurex.

known_facts_book1: A people of exactly one hundred and one, living on a Magic Isle in a lake at the far northern edge of the Gillikin Country, under a great glass Dome.
Look much like other Oz people, with beautiful homes, splendid clothes and ample food, but wear expressions of solemnity or nervous irritation — Dorothy sees at once that they are not happy.
Are terrorised by their own Queen, who hears every word spoken on the island and has them lashed at a whipping post for criticising her.
Cannot drown — they would only get wet and soggy and be very uncomfortable — but are helpless prisoners once the island sinks.
Own the fish of their lake and forbade the Flatheads to catch them, which is the whole origin of the war.
Were given their glass Dome and marble houses by the three Adepts, back when the two peoples were friends and visited each other freely.
Are told by Ozma to go home and do their daily tasks with patience, and are cheered amazingly by it; they get out their brass band and escort her to the palace.
**Elect their own Queen** at the end, choosing Lady Aurex, who is subject to Ozma in turn.
Cheer, wave hats and handkerchiefs and play the band as Ozma's party crosses the bridge home.

known_relations_book1.the Flatheads: Their enemies over the fish of the lake.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler they promise to obey.
